claims.text: The feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The previously used HVAF-i7 spray distance was longer than, and non-optimal relative to, approximately 300 mm.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
The increased particle velocity will raise particle kinetic energy at impact.
Higher impact energy will improve splat formation.
Higher impact energy will improve inter-particle bonding and coating consolidation.
Improved splat formation and consolidation will increase deposition efficiency.
Spraying at approximately 300 mm will produce a significantly thicker coating than the longer-distance baseline.
Spraying at approximately 300 mm will improve coating adhesion relative to the longer-distance baseline.
The shortened spray distance will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation because HVAF provides a low-oxidation environment.
The resulting coating will remain durable under high-temperature service conditions.
The intervention will remain effective for coating internal diameters down to 120 mm when parameters are tuned around a 300 mm spray distance.
The longer-distance HVAF-i7 baseline produced acceptable-quality coatings but inadequate thickness.
Operating at too short a distance or excessive impact conditions could cause uneven heating or reduced coating uniformity.
